title: Amazon Lab126 Clinic Project
text:
The Harvey Mudd College clinic program engages juniors and seniors in solving real-world, technical problems for companies and organizations. I was the team lead for Amazon Lab126’s clinic project for the 2023-2024 academic school year. Throughout the year, I lead a team of four students in a year long project to meet the requirements of the liaisons and clients. I utilized project management tools and developed team dynamics to maximize outcome performance. My team successfully simulated acoustic environments in the software tool Unity to enhance the performance of the Amazon Echo.

title: Somnia Collection - IDE Fundamentals Final Project
text:
This project was done in collaboration with OpenAI. We were asked by the design team to create an application of AI that goes beyond language models.
My team and I designed a sleep agent called Somnia. This device collects collection is designed to enhance the sleep experience by incorporating features such as a built in white noise machine, wireless charging, and a smart alarm clock that wakes you up with light instead of sound.


I also was in charge of creating a video advertisement for the product. I wrote the script, directed the video, and edited the final product.

title: LAIR Machine Learning Research Intern
text:
While working at the Laboratory for Autonomous and Intelligent Robotics (LAIR), I conducted research on the biomechanics of skateboarding, utilizing 3D calibration techniques to track and analyze movement in DeepLabCut.
First, my lab partner and I conducted secondary research on biomechanics and experimented position tracking in DeepLabCut.
We established an end-to-end workflow for data acquisition and analysis, which involved recording skateboarders and applying 3D calibration to extract meaningful insights from the captured footage.



Three Go Pro Camera Set Up for Calibration and Position Tracking


My work involved performing inverse dynamics to measure the kinematic forces exerted on joints, providing valuable insights into the physical demands of skateboarding.
This research not only deepened my understanding of biomechanics but also enhanced my ability to apply advanced analytical tools to real-world applications in robotics and human movement studies.
We also developed a lesson plan to be used by the professor in his biomechancs course, which included a detailed walkthrough of the data acquisition and analysis process, as well as the interpretation of results. This lesson plan aimed to educate students on the practical applications of machine learning in biomechanics and robotics.

With a passion for combining technical innovation with creative design thinking, I bring a unique perspective to solving complex challenges at the intersection of engineering and design.
When I’m not in the studio, I love to make music, run, and be outdoors!

title: Bladed Disk Simulation - E171 Final Project
text:
Modeled a bladed disk system as a chain of coupled spring–mass oscillators to study how structural variations affect vibration behavior in mechanical systems. Each oscillator represents a turbine blade, with stiffness representing blade flexibility and coupling springs representing interactions between neighboring blades.
Duration: October 2023 - December 2023 Team Size: 2 people




Approach We derived equations of motion for a 2DOF spring–mass system and extended the model to an N-degree-of-freedom system. We then formulated the system as a matrix eigenvalue problem, solved for natural frequencies and mode shapes in MATLAB for a 50-DOF system and analyzed the effect of varying the coupling ratio between blades.
Perfectly Periodic System We assumed that the blades were perfectly periodic, meaning that all blades had the same mass and stiffness. This allowed us to simplify the equations of motion and solve for the natural frequencies and mode shapes of the system.
